summary: Lab GPU kit rotation & conditional service-account retirement: equipment curation + access sunset plan
description:
Issue summary:
A scheduled rotation of developer lab GPU kits (laptops and 1U test nodes) is due for Q2. We need a coordinated plan to: 1) audit devices currently in the dev-lab pool, 2) reclaim and sanitize devices assigned to former contractors but still flagged as 'active', and 3) retire associated service accounts that were created for ephemeral workloads.

Impact:
- Potential data exposure if devices assigned to departed contractors still have active credentials or KMS access.
- Developer friction if hardware earmarked for rotation is not available during the onboarding wave starting 2026-04-01.
- Unclear ownership of several service accounts used by legacy test harnesses that could prevent identity clean-up or cause automation breakage if deleted without coordination.

Background / Context:
- Multiple offboarding tickets from last year referenced devices not returned (see linked issues).
- Inventory records (asset-tag CSV) diverge from the device management console by ~18 items for 'dev-lab' tag.
- Several service accounts named test-ephemeral-* have last-used timestamps older than 9 months; audit indicates some still have roles that grant access to staging KMS keys.

Requested action / Acceptance criteria:
- Reconcile dev-lab inventory: produce an authoritative CSV (asset_tag, serial, last_user, last_seen_date, location).
- Identify devices where last_user is a terminated or contractor user; schedule remote wipe or collection for physical return.
- Produce an access-sunset runbook for service accounts: categorize as (A) safe-to-delete, (B) require deprecation notice + 2-week freeze, (C) must be rotated instead of deleted.
- Coordinate with HR to confirm termination dates and with Solutions Eng to ensure no active CI jobs depend on accounts slated for deletion.
- Final sign-off from SRE and HR before any account is disabled.

Timeline / Constraints:
- Inventory reconciliation to be completed by 2026-03-10.
- Collection/wipe window: 2026-03-15 to 2026-03-29.
- Account retirement plan to be published by 2026-03-12.

Dependencies:
- HR termination exports and SCIM sync logs (HR owns export).
- DMZ courier scheduling for physical pickup in EMEA region.
- Solutions Eng to run a dry-check of CI jobs referencing test-ephemeral service accounts.

Risks:
- Deleting an account without proper deprecation notices could break internal automation.
- Devices wiped remotely that have unsynced local data could lose work.

Notes on policy question:
- This ticket should recommend whether to change the existing 30-day grace window for contractor account deactivation to 7 days for dev-lab assets, and propose an exception flow for long-running contractor engagements. The ticket should capture a concise policy draft for review by Security and People Ops.
checklist: Obtain HR termination CSV and SCIM last_sync (HR)
Export device last_seen + user from MDM (IT/Inventory)
Cross-reference inventory CSV with MDM and tag mismatches (Inventory)
Contact last_user and confirm device status or schedule collection (IT)
Classify service accounts and run dry-run dependency check (SRE/Infra)
Publish deprecation notices and set scheduled disable dates (IAM)
Execute wipe/collection and update asset tracker (IT/Logistics)
Post-action audit: confirm removed KMS roles and closed accounts (Security)
Document policy recommendation and circulate to Security + People Ops (Owner)
Close ticket when all items validated and confluence runbook updated (Owner)
